title: Would You Trust Your Lock Anymore? 😳 #engineering #technology #tools
description:
This Chinese tool is absolutely wild — it can both unlock and decode a lock in one compact device 👀

This video explains the working principle behind the Lishi Tool, a specialized locksmith tool designed for quickly opening and decoding automotive and standard locks without disassembly.

Invented by Li Zhi Qin, the tool combines two functions into a single compact mechanism: lock picking and key decoding. By applying light lifting force through a clever sliding lever system, the user can identify the binding pin inside the lock cylinder and determine the depth of each pin.

One particularly interesting detail is the floating pivot mechanism: the central pivot pin slides within a slot while simultaneously acting as the fulcrum of the lever system. This allows controlled force feedback during picking while also helping maintain accurate and evenly spaced measurement markings on the decoding scale. Once the pin depths are decoded using the built-in scale, a new key can be accurately cut from the measured values.

Different Lishi models are designed for specific lock profiles and keyways such as KW1, HU66, HU101, MIT11, TOY48, and many others.

🔑 Key Features:
• 2-in-1 lock pick and decoder tool
• Reads wafer depth directly from the lock
• Sliding pivot lever mechanism for lifting binding pins
• Designed for automotive and standard locks
• Fast decoding without lock disassembly

title: Why You Should Invest Early
description:
“The 20s are for fun 🤩 - I’ll invest in my 30s anyways!” 

If that’s your mindset, read ahead 👇🏻

Were you surprised to see the 1st child have a higher net worth than the 2nd child at the end of the reel? 💰

If you were wondering how it’s through the Power of COMPOUNDING 😎

For the first 10 years, boy no.1 chose to invest his INR 50,000 pocket money 💵 at an interest of 12%, earning him approximately INR 1.2 crores but then decided not to invest for the next 20 years. 

While the 2nd boy did the opposite and partied 🕺🏻 for the first 10 years and seriously invested for the next 20 years, finally earning him INR 5 crores. 

➡️ Here’s why the 1st boy earned more money in the end, even though he invested a lesser portion of the money gifted to him.

The answer is TIME !! 🕰️ 

While the 2nd boy was busy partying, the investments made by the first boy kept compounding. By the time the 2nd boy started investing, the 1st boy’s investments were already worth INR 1.2 crores. 💸

So no matter how long the 2nd boy keeps investing INR 50,000 monthly, the gap between them keeps growing even though the 1st boy stopped investing after the first 10 years. 

That’s how powerful compounding is 💪🏻 No wonder Albert Einstein called compounding the 8th wonder of the world 👏🏻

⚠️ Having fun is nice, but keep a portion of your income to invest from day 1 of earning money 🙌🏻

General Description & insights
The experiment aims to explore the concept of air occupying space and will engage students in discovering the presence and characteristics of this often-invisible substance. In this experiment, participants will conduct a series of hands-on activities to observe and measure the effects of air occupying space.

Using basic materials such as a syringe, water, and a plastic bottle or glass, participants will carefully fill the container with water, ensuring there is no air trapped inside. By attaching the syringe to the container and gradually retracting the plunger, the students will witness water being pushed out, indicating that the air inside the container is compressible and occupies space.

To further investigate this phenomenon, participants will explore the pressure exerted by air occupying space. They will seal the container with a balloon or cap and measure any changes in the balloon's size or cap's tightness as they alter the volume of air inside using the syringe.

title: Nepal Flood Isn’t Over! A New Lake Could Trigger Another Flood 🚨
description:
Nepal’s devastating flood may not be the end of the story. A new barrier lake formed after the glacier and rock collapse has raised concerns about possible secondary flooding in the Himalayas.

On August 26, a major ice-rock avalanche and debris flow triggered catastrophic flooding along the Bhote Koshi–Trishuli river system. The debris blocked river flow and contributed to the formation of temporary lakes upstream. Satellite imagery has since revealed newly formed water bodies, prompting authorities to closely monitor the situation.

The science is frighteningly simple:
Glacier collapse → debris blocks river → water accumulates → temporary lake forms → barrier failure can create another flood wave.

However, this does not mean another disaster on the scale of the August 26 flood is certain. Experts and authorities have been monitoring the lakes because the risk depends on how the barriers and water levels evolve.

This event highlights an important lesson for UPSC aspirants: Himalayan disasters are not only about rainfall. Glaciers, landslides, debris flows, temporary lakes, river systems, satellite monitoring and early-warning systems all matter.

Watch till the end to understand how one mountain collapse can create a second disaster risk.
